summary: A piece of fictional regional folklore about Willow's End, a fishing town haunted by the legend of the Vanishing Fisherman, a specter said to claim one lone fisherman every seven years. On September 15, 2023, the seventh year, Jacob Marrow sailed out alone to prove the tales were superstition and vanished, leaving his boat adrift. His disappearance divided the town into skeptics and believers and renewed the legend as a warning to respect the sea.
one_line: In the fishing town of Willow's End, fisherman Jacob Marrow vanishes at sea, seemingly fulfilling the legend of the Vanishing Fisherman who takes a victim every seven years.
key_facts: Willow's End is a fishing town where fog clings to the ships and many eerie tales and myths circulate, including sirens whose songs lure the unwary.
The legend says the Vanishing Fisherman is an eternal specter that claims the souls of those who challenge the sea.
According to the legend, a lone fisherman disappears into the mist every seven years and never returns.
Explanations of the ritual include the ocean's hunger, an offering to ancient gods dormant below, or the sea cleansing human insolence and pride.
Jacob Marrow, a middle-aged fisherman with weathered skin and grey eyes, set sail alone on September 15, 2023, to prove the tales were superstitions.
Jacob's boat was named the Sea Whisper.
Jacob's friends Eli Hastings and Mary Shaw watched him leave from the shore; it was the seventh year, with a blood-red moon, deathly still waters and haunting silence.
In the deepest part of the night, Jacob heard a melodious voice and felt a vast, ancient presence beneath the Sea Whisper, and unseen hands tugged at the boat as the water boiled.
The local coastguard found the Sea Whisper adrift the next morning with limp sails and a deck coated in eerie frost; there was no sign of Jacob.
Search parties combed the ocean by boat and by air but found no trace of Jacob Marrow.
Skeptics suggested accidental drowning or that Jacob fled his life in Willow's End, while believers said he was taken as the latest tribute.
The local newspaper 'The Coastal Echo' ran headlines blending fact and folklore, and old timers recalled similar past occurrences.
